taxonomyNote: Formerly Cervus unicolor; NatureServe notes Groves & Grubb (2011) place it in Cervus and that Rusa may not be monophyletic.
fieldMarks: Large; males 185-260 kg, females about 162 kg
Coarse dark coat with lighter brown to creamy underparts
Males have a dense neck mane and antlers with three or four tines up to 100 cm
Bushy tail white on the underside, raised as a signal
behavior: Mostly nocturnal; rests in dense cover by day
Solitary or in groups up to about 8 females
Browses at dusk and night on leaves, bark, berries and grass
habitat: Forested hillsides, swamp forest and open scrub, from sea level to about 3,700 m.
range: Native from India to southeastern China and the Malay Peninsula. Introduced and established in California, Texas and Florida (and Australia and New Zealand). Not native to Canada.
